title: P15.10-C R1: lease heartbeat + bounded claim-time lease lifetime + fenced post-await autonomous commit guard (F1 remediation)
description: R1 remediation on the same PR #87 branch (BASE 0e27bc6ee236d82633d4aee321ba9cd264adc0c3): a CEO model invocation can outlive the 60s lease TTL, and nothing revalidated autonomous authority inside the serialized post-await commit transaction. F1-B: scheduler.claim accepts an optional claim-time max_lifetime_ms bound (default 300s = P15.10-B behavior, min 60s, absolute cap 960s) persisted on the lease row and enforced by renew(); TTL stays 60s — never an unconditional raise. F1-A: the driver starts a bounded heartbeat ONLY after a valid claim — setInterval at DRIVER_HEARTBEAT_MS=20_000 (unref'd) calling the existing scheduler.renew(), which re-proves token/fence/worker-boot identity/claimed generation/expiry/policy-owner-terms-objective pins on every renewal; no heartbeat before claim, no lease creation, no DB write inside the 15s no-op window; retryable SQLite contention defers to the next tick while any other renewal fault marks the worker unauthorized (never assumes the external model call stopped) and aborts settlement; the timer is always stopped in `finally` so nothing leaks past settle/release/exception. F1-C: ceoCycle.runCycle accepts optional autonomous_commit_guard invoked FIRST inside the serialized store.immediate commit transaction — before re-observe, decision put, workstream decomposition, and attempt settle — so a revoke/pause/expiry landing mid-invocation rolls the entire commit back and the invoked attempt settles REJECTED through the existing canonical path (accounting preserved, terminal/UNKNOWN recovery semantics intact, no blind replay); runReview forwards it verbatim, pass() wires authorityGate into both CEO boundaries, and manual CEO callers are unchanged. F1-D: driver deps gain ceoTimeoutMs (env-validated 5_000..900_000 → claim bound = timeout+60s finalization allowance, capped 960s) and reconcileStaleAttempts(objectiveId) invoked pre-admission so a restart never re-invokes while an attempt is STARTED/UNKNOWN; serve-mission-control.mjs wires both from ceoCliTimeoutMs() + the lazily-composed default operating service's ceoCycle (createDefaultObjectiveOperatingService now also returns ceoCycle). Two-connection fencing proof: a stale handle cannot renew or settle after a new fence is claimed. No new CEO engine, no merge, no deploy — driver remains opt-in OFF.
